name: Eagle Syndrome

criteria.description: Radiographic evidence of styloid process elongation (>30 mm)
Persistent throat or pharyngeal pain exacerbated by head movement
Difficulty swallowing associated with styloid process elongation
Tenderness on palpation of the tonsillar fossa
Temporary pain relief after local anesthetic injection in the tonsillar region

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of styloid process elongation on imaging plus at least two major clinical symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by imaging; exclusion of other causes of oropharyngeal pain is essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elongated styloid process palpable in tonsillar fossa
searchTerms: long styloid bone felt in throat

pathognomonic.symptomName: Throat pain localized to tonsillar region
Pain exacerbated by head rotation or swallowing
searchTerms: discomfort with neck rotation or swallowing
feeling of something stuck in throat
pain felt in ear from throat issues

common.symptomName: Tenderness on palpation of tonsillar fossa

rare.symptomName: Syncope due to carotid artery compression
searchTerms: passing out due to neck artery compression
syncope caused by blood flow blockage

imaging: Elongated styloid process on panoramic radiograph or CT scan
Calcification of stylohyoid ligament on imaging
other: Tenderness on palpation of tonsillar fossa
Temporary pain relief after local anesthetic injection

distinguishingFeatures: Jaw clicking or limited mouth opening
Absence of elongated styloid process on imaging
Paroxysmal lancinating pain in glossopharyngeal nerve distribution
Trigger points in posterior tongue or throat
No styloid process elongation on imaging

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe neck or facial pain
Neurological deficits such as weakness or numbness
Syncope or signs of vascular compression
references: Eagle WW. Elongated styloid process: report of two cases. Arch Otolaryngol. 1937;25(5):584-587.
Murtagh RD, Caracciolo JT, Fernandez G. Eagle syndrome: clinical and radiographic findings. Am J Neuroradiol. 2001;22(7):1401-1402.
Piagkou M, Anagnostopoulou S, Kouladouros K, Piagkos G. Eagle syndrome: a review of the literature. Clin Anat. 2009;22(5):545-558.
